benefit_gate.rule: Pinned (default refresh model) beats the anchored control if, in every seed, its accuracy is higher or its mean freshness lag is lower, with zero leaks across seeds.
benefit_gate.reason: Pinned beat the anchored control in seeds 7 and 1234 but not in seed 42 (0.972 vs 0.986 accuracy, 0.033 vs 0.017 lag), so the rule fails without a leak: a tie. Mean accuracy 0.981 pinned vs 0.968 control at equal tokens; the control at full evidence scored 1.000, as did think. The anchoring is the measured win: at equal tokens it lifts query+reader from 0.884 to 0.968 accuracy and stale-wrong from 0.116 to 0.

default_decision: Pinned questions ship opt-in: gbrain creates no pin by itself, pinning a question is the owner consent for its paid refresh, and the standing_questions phase and context_pack delivery stay on for pins that exist (no setting changes). The anchored retrieval ships in pinned refresh (retrieveEvidence). Recommended next applications, each behind its own measured gate: query/search for entity-scoped latest-state questions, think gather for current-state questions about one entity, and context_pack entity cards.
cost_note: Pinned remains the cheapest correct answer for an entity question read often: at 100 reads per write $0.00057 per correct answer vs $0.00152 for the anchored reader at equal tokens and $0.00284 at full evidence; break-even about 110 reads per pin against the equal-token anchored reader and about 46 against the full-evidence one.
caveats: Synthetic seeded workload, 6 entities, 3 seeds; dev stage.
Every arm except query+reader at equal tokens is at or near the accuracy ceiling with embeddings on, so differences between them are within seed-to-seed variation.
Voyage embedding and rerank calls are not metered by the harness spend guard.

benefit_gate.reason: On the appended-corrections workload pinned answers with the default model were correct on 98.6% of reads versus 51.4% for query+reader and 79.2% for think, with 0% stale-wrong versus 48.6% and 20.8%. Mean freshness lag was 0.017 write batches versus 0.583 and 0.25. Zero leaks in 48 restricted-grant probes. Decision rule (set before the run): pinned beating query+reader on accuracy or freshness without leakage means default-on; it beats it on both.

run_2.default_decision: Pinned questions ship on. The standing_questions phase, publishing and context_pack delivery of fresh pinned answers are on by default (cycle.standing_questions.enabled=true, publish_mode=publish). Pinning a question remains the consent for its paid refresh, as plan C1 specifies, so no pin is created automatically and a brain with no pins makes no model call. Migrated dream.auto_think questions keep their old enabled, budget and auto_commit state. No shipped default changes relative to run 1; the verdict label moves from opt_in to default_on.
caveats: Retrieval asymmetry: the run-2 build anchors pinned refresh retrieval on the pin scope (entity page first, then pages that link to or name it, newest first). query+reader uses ordinary keyword query retrieval and think its own gather, both without that anchoring. The accuracy gap is partly this retrieval difference; a pin has a scope and an ad hoc query does not.
Keyword-only retrieval for every arm: the harness brain has no embedding key.

Cost: pinned with the default model costs more total dollars than query+reader until about 147 reads per pin (163 with the Sonnet refresh model). Per correct answer it costs 4.1x query+reader at 1 read per write, 0.59x at 10 and 0.24x at 100.
Withdrawal is the weakest event: 1 of 6 (default model) and 2 of 6 (Sonnet) pinned answers missed the revert after forget in batch 7.
Sonnet refresh returned non-JSON twice in 72 attempts (model_output_not_json); the pin kept its previous answer, which counts against it.

diagnostic_pre_fix_attempt.finding: Pinned refresh retrieval ranked every note sharing the question words alike and missed each entity newest note once notes accumulated, so pinned matched query+reader (0.528/0.542 vs 0.514 accuracy). Fixed in baadfc04 (src/core/questions/refresh.ts anchoredSlugs) with a regression test; not a decision input.

benefit_gate.reason: Accuracy is at ceiling for every arm (100% correct, 0 stale-wrong), so the gate is decided on lifecycle cost. Pinned costs 4.4x query+reader per correct answer at 1 read per write and matches it at 10 reads per write ($0.000526 vs $0.000529); break-even is about 240 reads per pin. Pinned is 3.3x (1 read/write) to 14.5x (10 reads/write) cheaper than on-demand think.

run_1.default_decision: Pinned questions ship opt-in: the feature does nothing until the owner pins a question, and no pin is created by default. Default-on is withheld because the benefit gate did not pass against query+reader.
run_1.ceiling_note: Every arm answered every read correctly; the workload rewrites the evidence page on correction, so no arm had a superseded value to repeat. The run cannot show an accuracy or freshness difference.
